absent: How coarse and fine-grained trap results combine into a final forward-or-handle decision.
Lookup order, priority and overlap resolution within and between the coarse and fine tables.
Locking, concurrency and caller context for consulting these tables.
Numeric encoding values and bit positions behind the named registers and controls.
Entries of the coarse table outside this tail fragment and of the fine table beyond part one.

findings.text: Nested coarse trap routing places breakpoint value and control families plus watchpoint value and control families across their full index spans, together with claim and authentication registers, under one debug trap selector combining TDE with TDA.

Operating-system lock and debug power-control behaviour is separated from general debug trapping: lock and power registers use TDE combined with TDOSA while the ROM address register uses TDE combined with TDRA.

Profiling and tracing registers are partitioned by feature: branch-record buffer controls under one selector, statistical sampling controls under a second, trace filter control under a third, and trace buffer base, limit, address, pointer, status and trigger under a fourth.

Activity-monitor EL0 controls, enable banks and counter and type banks share a CPTR TAM selector, CPACR uses a TCPAC selector, an encoding interval with fixed leading fields maps as a range to a TTA selector, timer registers split across physical versus virtual and timer versus counter selectors, and floating-point mode register uses an HCRX enable selector.

Guest interrupt-controller CPU-interface registers are split by affinity group and role: group-zero ordering, priority, acknowledge and enable state under one selector, group-one equivalents under a second, control and priority-mask state under a third, and deactivate under a combined fourth selector.

An implementation-defined choice treats virtualization SRE enable and select state as read-as-one and write-ignored, handles the relevant access locally, and never consults the outer enable state when deciding inner access, so guest observations are fixed regardless of outer configuration.

Fine-grained filter enumeration provides a no-filter sentinel, one selector for an HCRX XS-related condition, and a terminal count sentinel that must remain last, forming a small integer domain for conditional trap checks.

Each fine-grained trap row binds a start encoding and an end encoding, equal for single registers and distinct for intervals, to a descriptor holding a control-group selector, a bit position, a polarity value and an optional filter selector, plus a recorded source line; helper constructors fill the no-filter value when no filter is named.

Fine-grained routing spans general EL1 and EL0 registers under a first general group, alias and mask registers under a second general group, address-translate, TLB, cache and instruction-cache operations under a first instruction group, newer cache invalidate variants under a second instruction group, and performance, debug and branch-record registers under a debug group.
Fine-grained trap polarity uses value zero alongside negated control names and value one alongside direct control names.

TLB invalidate variants with a no-share qualifier reuse the same instruction-group control as their shareable counterparts but attach the HCRX XS-related filter for an extra outer-control check, while base variants carry no filter.
